prompt:
Write a first-person account (about 120 words) by the driver for an insurance claim form. Accident: low-speed head-on collision in League City, Texas. Injury: neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1362; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The claimant's account changed in important ways between conversations: the direction of the impact and the number of people in the car are now different.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
I was driving slowly through a residential stretch in League City when the car in front of me suddenly turned into my lane and we came together nose to nose. Neither of us was going fast, but the jolt was enough to throw me forward and back against the seat. My neck tightened up almost immediately, and by the next morning my lower back had joined in, so I have been dealing with a strain across both areas since then. I am the policyholder listed on this policy, and I have been cooperating with the adjuster from the start.

When I gave my first statement at the scene and in the days after, I described the impact and the people in the car as I remembered them at that time. As I have thought about it more and spoken with different people, some of those details have come into clearer focus, and I want to be open that my recollection of which way the force came from and how many people were riding along has shifted somewhat. I am not trying to hide that. I am simply trying to give the most accurate picture I can now, and I will answer any follow-up questions as fully as I am able.
